records.title: Track engine Slate visibility disagreement
records.reported_title: Slate snapshot and wait-for-text disagree on collapsed widgets (low)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Usability.
- **Scenario:** A menu row exists but is collapsed at runtime.
- **Reproduction status:** Observed once.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Open a menu in PIE where one row is collapsed by game logic.
  2. Wait for the row label text, then take a snapshot of all windows.
- **Observed:** The wait-for-text check returned true for the label. The snapshot did not list the label or its row.
- **Expected:** Both tools use the same visibility rule, or the snapshot marks collapsed widgets. User expectation.
- **Impact:** A first reading suggested the row was missing. More graph reads were needed to find that game logic collapses it.
- **State after:** No change.
- **Workaround:** Read the graph that sets the row visibility.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** Let the snapshot include collapsed widgets on request, with a visibility tag. This is an engine tool, not a TurboMCP tool. It is listed here because it affected the TurboMCP play workflow.
records.remaining: Compare current implementation and live help, then reproduce with generic project-owned fixtures; preserve the reported outcome and any failed run.

records.title: Preserve or explicitly transfer menu keyboard focus
records.reported_title: The focus action breaks widgets that read keys through their own key handler (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Usability.
- **Scenario:** A start screen widget reads "press any key" through its own key-down handler. It has keyboard focus at start.
- **Reproduction status:** Observed once, then avoided in two later runs.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Start PIE and wait for the start screen.
  2. Call EditTurboMCPPlayInput with the focus action, then send a gamepad face button hold.
- **Observed:** The focus action moved keyboard focus to the game viewport. Later key holds were delivered but not handled. The screen did not continue. A Slate click on the screen also did not continue it.
- **Expected:** A warning that the focus action takes focus from a focused menu widget. The result text says this only in general terms.
- **Impact:** One PIE run was lost. A restart was needed.
- **State after:** No asset change.
- **Workaround:** Restart PIE and do not call the focus action. The key then reached the widget. Worked.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** Report which widget had focus before the focus action and offer a mode that leaves menu focus alone.
records.remaining: Compare current implementation and live help, then reproduce with generic project-owned fixtures; preserve the reported outcome and any failed run.

records.title: Reconcile PIE activation and focus recovery
records.reported_title: Input is refused when the editor application is not the OS foreground application (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Limitation.
- **Scenario:** The user works in another application during a PIE test.
- **Reproduction status:** Repeated (4 times).
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Start PIE in a floating window.
  2. Give OS focus to another application, then send a hold.
- **Observed:** The tool returned that the editor application is inactive and sent no input. The engine Slate window select action did not make the application active.
- **Expected:** A way to activate the PIE window from the toolset, or input that does not need OS focus.
- **Impact:** Each case needed a manual step outside the toolset.
- **State after:** No change.
- **Workaround:** An external OS call brought the PIE window to the foreground. Worked each time.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** See FT-131.
records.remaining: docs/audit/play-activation-review.json already records activation action and unsuccessful OS foreground acquisition. This recurrence remains an explicit limitation, not a new proven repair.

records.title: Make suggested and reported node type IDs usable
records.reported_title: A refusal suggests a node type ID that the same tool then rejects (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Defect.
- **Scenario:** Add a self reference node to an event graph.
- **Reproduction status:** Observed once.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Call PreviewTurboMCPGraphAppend with a guessed self node ID. The refusal names a closest real ID.
  2. Call EditTurboMCPGraphAppend with that suggested ID.
- **Observed:** The edit refused the suggested ID as unknown and pointed to PreviewTurboMCPNodeType. That tool returned a different ID, which worked. The created-node report then printed the type under the first, refused ID.
- **Expected:** A suggested ID is accepted by the same tool. The documented contract says the closest IDs are real IDs.
- **Impact:** Two extra calls.
- **State after:** No change from the refused calls. The later append succeeded.
- **Workaround:** Use the ID from PreviewTurboMCPNodeType. Worked.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** Use one ID form in suggestions, creation reports and input.
records.remaining: Compare current implementation and live help, then reproduce with generic project-owned fixtures; preserve the reported outcome and any failed run.

records.title: Reconcile short node IDs across graph write tools
records.reported_title: Graph connect refuses short node IDs with a misleading message (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Defect.
- **Scenario:** Connect a new self node output to an existing getter input. Both short IDs came from tool results.
- **Reproduction status:** Repeated (2 times).
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Call EditTurboMCPGraphConnect with short node IDs and exact pin names.
  2. Call it again with the full asset, graph and ID form.
- **Observed:** The short form was refused with "pins must resolve uniquely in the named graph". Both pin names were correct, and PreviewTurboMCPNodePins confirmed them. The full form succeeded. Other tools in the same session accepted the short form.
- **Expected:** The same ID forms as the reader and node context tools, or a message that names the ID problem.
- **Impact:** Two refused calls and two pin checks.
- **State after:** No change from the refused calls.
- **Workaround:** Use the full ID form. Worked.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** Accept short IDs when they are unique, or say that the node ID did not resolve.
records.remaining: docs/audit/unique-edit-ids-review.json verifies GraphConnect short keys; GraphCopy review documents exact reader IDs. Field build unknown; compare each affected tool separately, not one assumed shared cause.

records.title: Track engine PIE stop state versus script errors
records.reported_title: A PIE stop call returned an error text and the session kept running (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Usability.
- **Scenario:** Stop PIE with the engine stop tool while project teardown logic raises a script error.
- **Reproduction status:** Repeated (3 stop calls in this session returned the same text; in one case PIE was still running).
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Start PIE, open a menu whose teardown raises a script error.
  2. Call the engine PIE stop tool, then a TurboMCP edit tool.
- **Observed:** The stop call returned the script error text as a tool error. In one case PIE was still running. The next EditTurboMCPFunctionAdd was refused because of the play session.
- **Expected:** The stop result says whether the session stopped, separate from script errors. User expectation.
- **Impact:** One refused edit and one extra check.
- **State after:** No asset change from the refused edit.
- **Workaround:** Confirm with the engine PIE state tool after each stop. Worked.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** This is an engine tool. TurboMCP edit refusals could name the running play session directly.
records.remaining: Compare current implementation and live help, then reproduce with generic project-owned fixtures; preserve the reported outcome and any failed run.

- **Workaround:** Clear plus Add on a member array. Worked.

records.title: Report complete pin container types and link mismatch reasons
records.reported_title: The pin tool reported a map output as a name (medium)

- **Expected:** The pin tool reports container types. The append refusal gives the type mismatch, as the connect tool does. User expectation.
- **Impact:** Three refused calls and one wrong design assumption.
- **State after:** No change from the refused previews.
- **Workaround:** EditTurboMCPGraphConnect to get the reason, then a map find node. Worked.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** Print the container kind in pin results. Reuse the connect refusal text in append preflight.
records.remaining: Compare current implementation and live help, then reproduce with generic project-owned fixtures; preserve the reported outcome and any failed run.

records.reported_title: No working tool path to shrink an array property on a data asset (medium)
records.observation:
- **Type:** Limitation.
- **Scenario:** An input mapping context asset with 65 mapping rows. One row (the last) had to be removed.
- **Reproduction status:** Observed once.
- **Steps to reproduce:**
  1. Open a checked-out input mapping context asset with more than one mapping row.
  2. Try to write the mappings array with one fewer row through the available property write tools.
- **Observed:** The array did not shrink. The row stayed in the asset.
- **Expected:** A property write with a shorter array removes the extra rows, or a dedicated remove-element operation exists. Basis: user expectation.
- **Impact:** One manual step in the editor. A to-do note had to be kept in the changelist description until the row was removed.
- **State after:** The asset was unchanged by the failed write. Unknown whether it was marked dirty.
- **Workaround:** Manual removal of the row in the editor. Worked.
- **Cause:** The cause is not confirmed.
- **Proposed behavior:** See FT-141.
